reader_question: How do women’s earnings compare with men’s in each state, and how sure is each figure?
grade_line: Documented: a Census Bureau survey, with ratios and their margins computed by Oath & Action
title: Women who worked full time, year round had median earnings 82.0 percent of men’s in 2025, and in 25 states and the District of Columbia the figure differed from the nation’s by more than the margin of error.
measure_line: Women’s median earnings as a percent of men’s, people 16 and over with earnings who worked full time, year round, 2025, 50 states and DC. Each line spans a figure’s 90 percent margin of error.
reading_guide: A filled dot differs from the nation’s 82.0 percent by more than the margin of error of the gap between them; an open dot sits within it.
notes: The ratio sets the median of every woman who worked full time, year round against the median of every such man, whatever their jobs.

A state differs from the nation where the gap between them passes the gap’s own margin of error, the square root of the sum of the two margins squared, the Census Bureau’s test. By that test, 13 states and the District of Columbia sit above the nation and 12 states below it. The chart lists the states by their figures; where two sit within each other’s margins, the order between them is not certain.
alt: Dots with margin of error lines for the 50 states and DC around the nation’s 82.0 percent. Fourteen filled dots above the nation’s line and 12 below it differ from it by more than the margin of error; the open dots of the other 25 states sit within it.
